extracted.intended_audience: school administrators and officials (PDSOs/DSOs) at institutions seeking or holding SEVP certification; legal/compliance staff managing SEVIS reporting and certification/recertification
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedures for SEVP certification, recertification, reporting to SEVIS, out-of-cycle reviews, withdrawal/denial processes, and related DSO/PDSO responsibilities under 8 CFR 214.3-214.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for reporting changes to SEVIS
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools must update SEVIS with the current information within 21 days of a change in any of the information contained in paragraphs (f)(1) and (h)(3) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also required to report within 21 days any change of the information contained in paragraph (g)(1) or the occurrence of specified events (see related metric for list of events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Events requiring 21-day reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools are required to report within 21 days the occurrence of: any student who has failed to maintain status or complete his or her program; a change of the student's or dependent's legal name or U.S. address; any student who has graduated early or prior to the program end date listed on SEVIS Form I-20; any disciplinary action taken by the school against the student as a result of the student being convicted of a crime; and any other notification request not covered by paragraph (g)(1) made by DHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For F-1 students authorized a 24-month OPT extension under 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C): report (1) changes student reports concerning legal name, residential or mailing address, employer name, or employer address; and (2) the end date of the student's employment reported by a former employer per 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(C)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term/session registration reporting (30-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each term or session and no later than 30 days after the deadline for registering for classes, schools are required to report registration information including whether the student has enrolled, dropped below a full course of study without prior authorization by the DSO, or failed to enroll; the current address of each enrolled student; and the start date of the student's next session, term, semester, trimester, or quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For initial students, the start date is the 'program start date' or 'report date'; DSOs may choose a reasonable date but not more than 30 days prior to start of classes. Adjustments to the program completion date must reflect factors influencing progress (deferred attendance, authorized drop below, program extension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative correction of SEVIS records
rubrics_metrics.description: In instances where technological or computer problems on the part of SEVIS cause an error in the student's record, the DSO may request the SEVIS system administrator, without fee, to administratively correct the student's record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this process for SEVIS-caused errors; does not waive other reporting responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SEVIS and Form I-17 for certification filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A school seeking SEVP certification must use SEVIS to file an electronic petition (which compiles the data for the Form I-17) and must submit the nonrefundable certification petition fee on-line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The school must access the SEVP website to file, will be issued a temporary SEVIS user ID and password to complete and submit an electronic Form I-17, and must submit the proper nonrefundable fee as provided in 8 CFR 103.7(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Site visit requirement for certification
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP will conduct a site visit for each petitioning school and its additional schools or campuses. The school must comply with and complete the visit within 30 days after the date SEVP contacts the school to arrange the visit, or the petition for certification will be denied as abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DSOs and officials who have signed the Form I-17 must be able to demonstrate how they obtain access to the regulations cited in the petition and extract pertinent citations; paper or electronic access acceptable. SEVP will serve notice of approval and update SEVIS if authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification denial notice procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP will serve a notice of denial in accordance with paragraph (f)(2) of this section if a school's petition for certification is denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial notice will inform the petitioning school of the reasons and its appeal rights per 8 CFR 103.3(a)(1)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recertification filing deadlines and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools are required to file a completed petition for SEVP recertification before the school's certification expiration date (which is 2 years from the date of previous certification or recertification) and must submit the proper nonrefundable recertification petition fee as provided in 8 CFR 103.7(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEVP will notify DSOs 180 days prior to expiration that the school may submit a petition; a school may file at any time after that notification but must submit a complete recertification petition package by its certification expiration date. SEVP will send a notice of confirmation of complete filing or rejection upon receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of confirmation or rejection of recertification filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of confirmation assures a school of uninterrupted access to SEVIS while SEVP adjudicates the school's petition; a school that has complied will continue to have SEVIS access after its certification expiration date while adjudication is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A school is required to comply with all regulatory recordkeeping, retention, reporting and other requirements during the period the petition is pending. Notice of rejection requires prompt corrective action to ensure acceptance for adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of failure to petition for recertification
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP will serve a Notice of Intent to Withdraw (NOIW) 30 days prior to a school's certification expiration date. SEVP will no longer accept a petition and will immediately withdraw the school's certification if the school does not petition for recertification, abandons its petition, or does not submit a complete petition package by the expiration date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon withdrawal the school must comply with 8 CFR 214.4(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recertification assessment focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment by SEVP of a school petitioning for recertification will focus primarily on overall school compliance, but may also include examination of individual DSO compliance as data and circumstances warrant; past performance of individuals will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if individuals no longer serve as PDSOs/DSOs, their past performance may be considered in recertification.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-site review requirement for recertification
rubrics_metrics.description: All schools are subject to on-site review, at the discretion of SEVP, in conjunction with recertification. The school must comply with and complete an on-site review within 30 days of notification by a DHS representative, or the petition for recertification will be denied as abandoned, resulting in withdrawal from SEVIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to complete timely triggers denial as abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recertification approval and cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP will serve a notice of approval if a school's petition for recertification is approved. The date of the subsequent recertification review will be two years after the school's certification expiration date from this petition cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recertification denial procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP will serve a notice of denial if a school's petition for recertification is denied, in accordance with 8 CFR 103.3(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Out-of-cycle review triggers (Form I-17 changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP will determine if out-of-cycle review is required upon receipt in SEVIS of any changes from an SEVP-certified school to its Form I-17 information. Changes that require out-of-cycle review when changed include approval for attendance of students (F/M/both); name of school system; name of main campus; mailing address; location of the school; school type; public/private indicator; private school owner name; the school is engaged in (activity); operating authorizations; accreditation approvals; areas of study; degrees available; whether engaged in elementary/secondary/higher/vocational/technical/English language training; adding or deleting campuses; campus name; campus mailing address; and campus location address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an extensive list (A–T) of Form I-17 fields that, when changed, may trigger immediate SEVP review.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVP requests for updates and documentation (10 business days)
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP may request a school to electronically update all Form I-17 fields in SEVIS and provide SEVP with documentation supporting the update. The school must complete such updates in SEVIS and submit supporting documentation to SEVP within 10 business days of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely comply can trigger further review or withdrawal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVP authority to review and initiate remedial/withdrawal action
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP may review a school's certification at any time to verify compliance with recordkeeping, retention, reporting and other requirements and may initiate remedial action with the school, as appropriate, and may initiate withdrawal proceedings pursuant to 8 CFR 214.4(b) if noncompliance or ineligibility is identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews can occur at any time based on SEVIS data or other information.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-site review and withdrawal proceedings for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP-certified schools are subject to on-site review at any time. SEVP will initiate withdrawal proceedings pursuant to 8 CFR 214.4(b) if the certified school selected for on-site review prior to its certification expiration date fails to comply with and complete the review within 30 days of notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Continued Eligibility after out-of-cycle review
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP will serve a Notice of Continued Eligibility if, upon completion of an out-of-cycle review, SEVP determines that the school remains eligible for certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such notice will not change the previously-determined certification expiration date unless specifically notified by SEVP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of certification and voluntary withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP will institute withdrawal proceedings if, upon completion of an out-of-cycle review, SEVP determines that a school or its programs are no longer eligible for certification. A school can voluntarily withdraw from SEVP certification at any time or in lieu of complying with an out-of-cycle review or request; failure to comply will be treated as voluntary withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To initiate voluntary withdrawal, the school must send a request on official school letterhead to SEVP.

rubrics_metrics.name: DHS campus reviews for student regulation compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS officials may conduct out-of-cycle, on-site reviews on the campuses of SEVP-certified schools to determine whether nonimmigrant students are complying with DHS regulations pertaining to them, including the requirement that each maintains a valid passport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS officers will take appropriate action regarding violations of the regulations by nonimmigrant students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising statement limitation for SEVP-certified schools
rubrics_metrics.description: In any advertisement, catalogue, brochure, pamphlet, literature, or other material printed or reprinted by or for an SEVP-certified school, any statement concerning certification for attendance by nonimmigrant students shall be limited solely to the following: 'This school is authorized under Federal law to enroll nonimmigrant alien students.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No other certification-related statements are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of Form I-20 (Certificate of Eligibility) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A DSO of an SEVP-certified school must sign any completed Form I-20 issued for a prospective or continuing student or a dependent. A Form I-20 issued by a certified school system must state which school within the system the student will attend. Only a DSO of an SEVP-certified school may issue a Form I-20 and only after specified conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions to issue: (1) prospective student has made a written application; (2) the written application, transcripts/records, proof of financial responsibility, and other supporting documents have been received, reviewed, and evaluated at the school's U.S. location; (3) appropriate authority has determined qualifications meet admission standards; (4) the official responsible for admission has accepted the prospective student for enrollment in a full course of study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and qualification of Designated Official (DSO/PDSO)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Designated Official, DSO, or PDSO means a regularly employed member of the school administration whose office is located at the school and whose compensation does not come from commissions for recruitment of foreign students. An individual whose principal obligation to the school is to recruit foreign students for compensation does not qualify. The PDSO and any other DSO must be named by the president, owner, or head of a school or school system. The PDSO and DSO may not delegate this designation to any other person.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDSO/DSO citizenship and campus responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A PDSO and DSO must be either a citizen or lawful permanent resident of the United States. Each campus must have one PDSO. The PDSO is responsible for updating SEVIS to reflect the addition or deletion of any DSO on their associated campus. SEVP will use the PDSO at the main campus as the point of contact on compliance issues and system alerts. The PDSO of the main campus is the only DSO authorized to submit a Form I-17 for recertification. SEVP may designate certain SEVIS functions for PDSO use only. PDSO and DSO share responsibilities in all other respects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination and SEVIS access for DSOs
rubrics_metrics.description: School officials may nominate as many DSOs as necessary to provide recommendations to F and/or M students and to support timely recordkeeping and reporting. School officials must not permit a DSO or PDSO nominee access to SEVIS until DHS approves the nomination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition inclusion and update requirements for designated officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for SEVP certification, review and recertification must include the names, titles, and signatures of designated officials. A certified school must update SEVIS upon any changes to persons who are principal or designated officials, and furnish the name, title and e-mail address of any new official within 21 days of the change. Any changes to the PDSO or DSO must be made by the PDSO within 21 days of the change. DHS may, at its discretion, reject the submission of any individual as a DSO or withdraw a previous submission by a school of an individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of designated officials required
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for school certification must include a statement by each designated official certifying that the official is familiar with DHS regulations relating to admission and maintenance of nonimmigrant students, change of nonimmigrant status under part 248, and school certification under §§ 214.3 and 214.4, and affirming the official's intent to comply with these regulations. At the time a new designated official is added, the designated official must make the same certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for denial of recertification or withdrawal (enumerated grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP certification will be withdrawn on notice or recertification denied if the school or school system is determined no longer entitled to certification for any valid and substantive reason, including (but not limited to) failures such as: failure to comply with 8 CFR 214.3(g)(1) without a subpoena; failure to comply with 8 CFR 214.3(g)(2); failure of a DSO to notify SEVP of attendance of an F-1 transfer student; failure to identify on the Form I-20 which school within the system the student must attend; willful issuance by a DSO of a false statement; DSO conduct not complying with regulations; designation of unqualified individuals as DSO; failure to provide SEVP with Form I-17 bearing names/titles/signatures of DSOs; failure to submit statements of DSOs; issuance of Form I-20 without proof of scholastic, language, or financial requirements; issuance to aliens not enrolled or not carrying full courses; failure to operate as a bona fide institution of learning; failure to employ adequate qualified personnel; failure to limit advertising as prescribed; failure to maintain proper facilities, accreditation/licensing, physical plant, curriculum, teaching staff as represented in Form I-17; failure to comply with procedures for issuance of Form I-20; failure of a DSO to notify SEVP of material changes (name, address, curricular changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an illustrative, non-exhaustive list of substantive reasons that can support denial or withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic withdrawal criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: SEVP certification will be automatically withdrawn: (i) as of the date of termination of operations if an SEVP-certified school terminates operations; (ii) as of a school's certification expiration date if it does not submit a completed recertification petition as required; (iii) sixty days after a change of ownership if the school failed to update its information in accordance with § 214.3(h)(1) or properly file a new petition (SEVP will review any proper petition filed); (iv) if an SEVP-certified school voluntarily withdraws from its certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A school that is automatically withdrawn may file a new petition at any time and past compliance will be considered in evaluating subsequent petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal on notice (NOIW) procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If SEVP has information that a school may no longer be entitled to certification, SEVP will serve an NOIW informing the school of: the grounds for withdrawing SEVP certification; the 30-day deadline to submit sworn statements and documentary or other evidence to rebut the grounds; and the school's right to request a telephonic interview in support of its response within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An NOIW is not a means to submit evidence that should have previously been submitted under established reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to counsel during NOIW/withdrawal process
rubrics_metrics.description: The school or school system shall be informed in the notice of intent to withdraw certification that it may be assisted or represented by counsel of its choice qualified under part 292 of this chapter, at no expense to the Government, in preparation of its answer or in connection with the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of admitting allegations or failing to answer NOIW
rubrics_metrics.description: If the school admits all allegations in the NOIW, or fails to file an answer within the 30-day period, SEVP will withdraw the certification previously granted and notify the designated school official of the decision. No appeal will be accepted if all allegations are admitted or no answer is filed within the 30-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements if allegations are denied
rubrics_metrics.description: If the school denies the allegations in the NOIW, then the school shall, in its answer, provide all information or evidence on which the answer is based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview procedures during withdrawal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the school requests an interview in its answer, the school will be given notice of the date set. A summary of the information provided at the interview will be prepared and included in the record. At SEVP's discretion, the interview may be recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision standard and appeals timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision of SEVP will be in accordance with 8 CFR 103.3(a)(1). A school may file an appeal of a denial or withdrawal no later than 15 days after the service of the decision by ICE; the appeal must state the reasons and grounds and be accompanied by the fee as provided in 8 CFR 103.7(d)(15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operations and obligations when certification relinquished/withdrawn or recertification denied
rubrics_metrics.description: A school whose certification is relinquished or withdrawn, or whose recertification is denied may, at SEVP discretion, no longer be able to create Initial student records or issue new Form I-20 for initial attendance. Schools must comply with instructions given in the notice regarding management of status for Initial and continuing F and/or M students. All other SEVIS functionality, including event reporting for students, will remain unchanged until the school's SEVIS access termination date. The school must continue to comply with recordkeeping, retention, reporting and other requirements until its SEVIS access termination date.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS access termination considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the SEVIS access termination date, SEVP will consider the impact on SEVP, the school, and the school's nonimmigrant students. In most situations SEVP will not determine a SEVIS access termination date until appeals have concluded unless the school is suspected of criminal activity or poses a potential national security threat. The school will no longer be able to access SEVIS, and SEVP will automatically terminate any remaining Active SEVIS records for that school on the SEVIS access termination date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal obligations and consideration for future petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools are obligated to their students to provide the programs of study to which they committed and are obligated to the U.S. government to comply with recordkeeping, retention, reporting and other requirements of 8 CFR 214.3. With any new petition for SEVP certification, SEVP will consider the extent to which a school has fulfilled these obligations during any previous period of certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of status and benefit prohibitions for Libyan nationals/agents
rubrics_metrics.description: The nonimmigrant status of any Libyan national, or any other foreign national acting on behalf of a Libyan entity, engaging in aviation maintenance, flight operations, or nuclear-related studies or training is terminated. The following benefits will not be available to such persons where the purpose is to engage in those activities: application for school transfer, application for extension of stay, employment authorization or practical training, request for reinstatement of student status, and application for change of nonimmigrant status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a categorical bar subject to the terms set out in § 214.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: USMCA professional-level temporary entry definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 214(e) and the USMCA, a citizen of Canada or Mexico seeking temporary entry as a business person to engage in business activities at a professional level must demonstrate business activity at a professional level as defined by Appendix 2 to Annex 16-A of Chapter 16 of the USMCA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business activities at a professional level means those undertakings requiring at least a baccalaureate degree or appropriate credentials demonstrating status as a professional as listed in Appendix 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profession-specific minimum qualification requirements (USMCA Appendix 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix 2 lists professions and the minimum requirements for qualification for each (examples include: Accountant — Baccalaureate or Licenciatura Degree; or C.P.A./C.A./C.G.A./C.M.A.; Architect — Baccalaureate or Licenciatura Degree or state/provincial license; Computer Systems Analyst — Baccalaureate or Licenciatura Degree or Post-Secondary Diploma/Certificate and three years experience; and many others including medical/allied professionals with specified degrees or licenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking admission under USMCA must demonstrate professional-level activity in one of the listed professions and meet the listed minimum qualifications for that profession.
